verses.9:2: {confitebor}, Senhor, de todo o meu coração: * narrarei todas as vossas maravilhas.
verses.9:3: Eu me alegrarei e exultarei em vós: * {psallam}.
verses.9:5: Porque {v5a} e a minha causa: * sentastes-vos sobre o trono, vós que julgais {justitiam}.
verses.9:6: {increpasti} as nações, e pereceu o ímpio: * apagastes o nome deles {v6end}.
verses.9:7a: As espadas do inimigo {defecerunt} {finem}: * e destruístes as cidades deles.
verses.9:7b: Pereceu a memória deles com estrondo: * e o Senhor permanece {aet}.
verses.9:8b: Preparou o seu trono {in_judicio}: * e ele mesmo julgará {orbem} com equidade, julgará os povos com justiça.
verses.9:11: E esperem em vós os que conhecem o vosso nome: * porque não abandonastes os que vos buscam, Senhor.
verses.9:12: Entoai salmos ao Senhor, que habita em Sião: * anunciai entre as nações {studia}:
verses.9:13: Porque, {requirens}, ele se lembrou: * não esqueceu o clamor {pauper2}.
verses.9:14: Tende piedade de mim, Senhor: * vede {humilitatem} {de_inimicis}.
verses.9:15: Vós que me {exaltas} das portas da morte, * para que eu anuncie todos os vossos louvores nas portas da filha de Sião.
verses.9:16a: Exultarei na vossa salvação: * as nações {infixae} na {interitu}.
verses.9:16b: Neste laço que esconderam, * {comprehensus} o pé deles.
verses.9:18: {convertantur} os pecadores para {infernum}, * todas as nações que esquecem a Deus.
verses.9:20: Levantai-vos, Senhor, não {confortetur} o homem: * sejam julgadas as nações {conspectu}.
verses.9:21: Estabelecei, Senhor, {legislatorem} sobre eles: * para que as nações saibam que são homens.

decisions.why: D5 settles confitéri (to God) → dar graças a; 9:2 is the psalm's first word and the same colon opens 110:1 and 137:1 (Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo — grep). The only question is how the dative pronoun sits: the Latin puts tibi second, and Portuguese has three places for vos.

options.label: Eu vos darei graças
options.note: Ruling. The pronoun before the verb, as Brazilian speech puts it, with the subject pronoun supplied (D2) so that the verse does not open on an unstressed vos. Keeps D5's dative (vos = tibi), as Ps 6:6 'quem vos dará graças'. Sixteen syllables for the Latin's seventeen.

options.label: Darei graças a vós
options.note: The Latin's order of verb and pronoun, with the stressed form; natural too, a little heavier on 'vós' before the vocative (a vós, Senhor).

options.label: Dar-vos-ei graças
options.note: Mesóclise: correct, and what a printed psalter of the last century would have; the brief allows it only where it reads naturally, and in current Brazilian speech it does not.

options.label: Eu vos glorificarei
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 ('Eu te glorificarei'). Refused by D5: glorificáre has its own word (glorificar, Ps 90:15).

decisions.why: psállere → entoar salmos (D25), with the dative kept (ao vosso nome). The Latin ends on the vocative Altíssime, a proparoxytone; the brief wants the final word stressed on its last or second-last syllable, and Ps 7:18 was re-ordered for the same word at the stylist's request. The vocative is bare, as the glossary's rule for Senhor and Deus has it (no 'ó' unless the Latin has 'o').

options.label: Altíssimo, entoarei salmos ao vosso nome

forms.psallam: Altíssimo, entoarei salmos ao vosso nome

options.note: Ruling since draft 2, the stylist’s: the vocative opens the colon, so that the verb runs on to its dative without a break; order only (D2). It stands right after ‘em vós’, so it is heard as said to God. The verse still closes on ‘nome’.

options.label: entoarei salmos, Altíssimo, ao vosso nome

forms.psallam: entoarei salmos, Altíssimo, ao vosso nome

options.note: Draft 1: the vocative inside the colon. Refused by the stylist: it parts the singing from its object and the phrase must start again after it.

options.label: entoarei salmos ao vosso nome, Altíssimo

forms.psallam: entoarei salmos ao vosso nome, Altíssimo

options.note: The Latin's order; ends on a proparoxytone, the Latin's own stress (Altíssime).

options.label: entoarei salmos ao vosso nome, ó Altíssimo

forms.psallam: entoarei salmos ao vosso nome, ó Altíssimo

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and the CNBB both put 'ó'; the glossary keeps the bare vocative unless the Latin has 'o'.

decisions.why: A gerund with an accusative: 'in the turning my enemy back'. Who turns him is not said; the Greek (ἐν τῷ ἀποστραφῆναι τὸν ἐχθρόν μου εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω) is a passive infinitive, Douay-Rheims 'When my enemy shall be turned back', Matos Soares 1932 makes God the agent ('porque puseste em fuga os meus inimigos'). convértere → voltar (glossary); retrórsum → 'para trás' — not 'atrás': 'voltar atrás' is the idiom for going back on one's word.

options.label: Ao fazer voltar para trás o meu inimigo

forms.convertendo: Ao fazer voltar para trás o meu inimigo

options.note: Ruling since draft 2, the Latinist’s (major): the gerund is active with inimícum meum as its object — someone turns the enemy back. ‘fazer voltar’ says that and still names no one: the agent stays the Latin’s silence (the second colon’s ‘diante da vossa face’ points to God, as in the Latin). The stylist’s line (option 2) makes the enemy the subject, which is the Greek’s passive read as the Latin is not.

options.label: Ao voltar para trás o meu inimigo

forms.convertendo: Ao voltar para trás o meu inimigo

options.note: Draft 1: ‘ao’ + infinitive with the enemy heard as the one who turns — the Latinist marked it major (the accusative is the object of the gerund), and the stylist heard the subject arrive late.

options.label: Quando o meu inimigo voltar para trás

forms.convertendo: Quando o meu inimigo voltar para trás

options.note: The stylist’s line for draft 1 (the subject first). It makes the verb intransitive, which the Latin’s accusative does not allow — refused on the Latinist’s ground.

options.label: Quando fizerdes voltar para trás o meu inimigo

forms.convertendo: Quando fizerdes voltar para trás o meu inimigo

options.note: Names God as the agent, with Matos Soares 1932 — resolves what the Latin leaves open.

options.label: Quando o meu inimigo for voltado para trás

forms.convertendo: Quando o meu inimigo for voltado para trás

options.note: Douay-Rheims' passive, to the letter; heavy.

decisions.why: A future passive (the Greek has the active ἀσθενήσουσιν, ‘they will be weak’). The Latinist (v1, inside his major on 9:4) asks for the voice. glossary: infírmus row — infirmári → enfraquecer.

options.label: serão enfraquecidos
options.note: Ruling since draft 2: the Latin’s voice (Douay-Rheims ‘they shall be weakened’). Cost: the colon is now five syllables over the Latin’s — accepted for the voice; ‘à vossa face’ in decision a_facie would take three back.

options.label: enfraquecerão
options.note: Draft 1: the intransitive, which is the Greek’s active and Matos Soares 1932’s ‘serão debilitados’ in another shape; shorter.

decisions.why: a fácie = ἀπὸ προσώπου, 'from before the face'. The glossary has 'da face de' for a fácie terræ (1:4, where something is driven off the face of the earth); 'perecerão da vossa face' is not Portuguese. Douay-Rheims 'before thy face', Matos Soares 1932 'diante de ti'.

options.label: diante da vossa face
options.note: Ruling. Keeps the face (rule 5) and the glossary's 'face'; 'diante de' is what Douay-Rheims reads.

options.label: à vossa face
options.note: The Diurnal's diction ('sucumbem à tua face'); shorter, a shade literary.

options.label: longe da vossa face
options.note: Says the 'from' of the preposition, but supplies 'longe'.

decisions.why: fácere judícium (open glossary row: 118:84 'fazer juízo sobre', 118:121 'praticar o juízo'). Here the judgment is the speaker's own, set beside causam meam — the glossary row judicáre names 9:5 as a verse that must decide locally. The sense is 'you have done me justice in my case' (Douay-Rheims 'maintained my judgment'; the Greek τὴν κρίσιν μου καὶ τὴν δίκην μου). judícium → juízo is settled (D15); but 'o meu juízo' alone is heard as 'my opinion' or 'my good sense' (the blind reader at 118:154), so the verb must make the legal sense audible.

options.label: fizestes valer o meu juízo
options.note: Ruling. Keeps fácere as 'fazer' and judícium as 'juízo'; 'fazer valer' is the living idiom for enforcing a right ('fazer valer os seus direitos'), so the legal sense is heard. Cost: 'valer' is supplied — Matos Soares 1932 supplies a verb too ('defendeste').

options.label: defendestes o meu juízo
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's verb; clear, but replaces fácere.

options.label: sustentastes o meu direito
options.note: The CNBB's line (from the Hebrew) and Douay-Rheims' verb: the plainest Portuguese, but it leaves D15's 'juízo' for a second word.

options.label: fizestes o meu juízo
options.note: The calque; heard as 'you formed my opinion'.

decisions.why: An accusative of content, as the Greek (ὁ κρίνων δικαιοσύνην): 'who judge justice', i.e. judge justly. Douay-Rheims keeps it ('who judgest justice'); Matos Soares 1932 makes it an adverbial ('segundo a justiça'). 9:8b has the other build (in justítia → com justiça), so the two should not be made one.

options.label: a justiça
options.note: Ruling. The Latin's object kept, as Douay-Rheims keeps it; the verse stays a shade odd, as the Latin is, and stays apart from 9:8b's 'com justiça'.

options.label: com justiça
options.note: What the phrase means, in the build of 9:8b — merges two Latin constructions.

options.label: segundo a justiça
options.note: Matos Soares 1932.

decisions.why: increpáre → repreender (working); since D21 it shares the word with árguere, and D21 asks whether a better word appears for God's rebuke of the nations — this is the place. The Greek is ἐπετίμησας (rebuke; in the Gospels also 'rebuke the wind'). 118:21 'Increpásti supérbos' is the same build and reads 'Repreendestes os soberbos'. Douay-Rheims 'rebuked', Matos Soares 1932 'repreendeste'; the CNBB (from the Hebrew) has 'Ameaçaste'.

options.label: Repreendestes
options.note: Ruling: the glossary word holds. It is what both Vulgate-family versions have, and 9:6 then says what 118:21 says. No better word turned up for the nations: 'ameaçar' is a threat not yet carried out, where here the nations perish in the same breath; 'increpar' is the cognate but a dictionary word. The split from árguere can still be made where the rebuke is a blast (ab increpatióne tua fúgient, 103:7; 17:16b, 75:7, 79:17) — there a noun is wanted and 'repreensão' is weak.

options.label: Ameaçastes
options.note: The CNBB's diction (from the Hebrew); one of the senses of ἐπιτιμάω. It would restore the split from árguere, but a threat is less than the Latin says, and it is not the Vulgate family's word.

options.label: Increpastes
options.note: The cognate; exists in the dictionary, needs a footnote in the pew.

decisions.why: Settled by D23: in ætérnum → para sempre, one with in sǽculum (εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα). 9:37 (second stage) has the phrase again.

options.label: eternamente
options.note: The glossary's word before D23; heavy (five syllables) at the end of 9:7b.

decisions.why: The formula row in sǽculum (in ætérnum) et in sǽculum sǽculi names 9:6. D23: 'where they stand together the second member is pelos séculos dos séculos'. The Latinist asked twice in Ps 118:44 for the singular. The slot takes in the whole phrase so that the stylist’s reversal can be shown.

options.label: para sempre, e pelos séculos dos séculos
options.note: Ruling: the glossary formula, the words every Brazilian Catholic knows from the doxology’s close. The Latinist (v1, minor) asks again for the singular, as in 118:44 — refused for the same reason: ‘pelo século do século’ is not said in Portuguese prayer; the Greek has the plural in the first member of other places and the Latin’s singular is a Hebraism kept by every Vulgate-family version in the plural (Douay-Rheims ‘for ever and ever’, Matos Soares 1932 ‘dos séculos’).

options.label: para sempre, e pelo século do século
options.note: The Latin’s singular, as the Latinist asks (118:44, and here again, minor).

options.label: para sempre, e por todos os séculos dos séculos

forms.v6end: {aet}, e por todos os séculos dos séculos

options.note: Matos Soares 1932; ‘todos’ supplied.

options.label: pelos séculos dos séculos, e para sempre
options.note: The stylist’s line for draft 1, to end on a paroxytone. Refused: it reverses the Latin’s two members (in ætérnum comes first), and the Latin itself ends on the proparoxytone sǽculi — the formula is kept whole, as the brief keeps formulas.

decisions.why: defícere → desfalecer (glossary row deféctio / defícere, open; Ps 118:81 'A minha alma desfaleceu'). Here the subject is swords (ἐξέλιπον αἱ ῥομφαῖαι): they 'failed, gave out'. Douay-Rheims 'failed'; Matos Soares 1932 changes the image ('ficaram embotadas'). inimíci is a genitive singular with the Greek (τοῦ ἐχθροῦ) and Douay-Rheims.

options.label: desfaleceram
options.note: Ruling. The glossary verb, used of things as Portuguese allows ('as forças desfaleceram'): the swords give out as a man's strength gives out. Keeps one Latin verb one Portuguese verb.

options.label: falharam
options.note: Douay-Rheims' 'failed'; plain, but in Brazil a thing that 'falha' is first of all a thing that malfunctions.

options.label: ficaram embotadas
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: a blunted edge is another image.

decisions.why: in finem (εἰς τέλος) stands three times in Ps 9 (9:7a, 9:19 twice; 9:32 in the second stage) beside in ætérnum (9:6, 9:7b, 9:37), and 19 verses in the psalter (grep; 12:1 obliviscéris me in finem, 73:1, 73:19 …). By D15's test the two phrases are different Greek (εἰς τέλος / εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα) and Portuguese has a plain second phrase, so they stay apart. In 9:19 the Greek has εἰς τέλος then εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, and the Latin repeats in finem: the repetition is the Latin's and is kept. Douay-Rheims 'unto the end' (9:7a, 9:19a, 9:32); Matos Soares 1932 'para sempre' throughout.

options.label: até o fim
options.note: Ruling, proposed for the glossary. The Latin's noun (finis → fim) and Douay-Rheims' reading; it keeps in finem apart from in ætérnum in a psalm that has both three times, and the repetition of 9:19 is heard as the Latin's.

options.label: para sempre
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. The idiom a Portuguese ear expects in 9:19 ('não será para sempre esquecido'), but it merges in finem with in ætérnum, which the psalm sets a verse apart (9:6–9:7b).

decisions.latin: Quóniam non in finem oblívio erit páuperis
decisions.why: The Latin puts ‘non in finem’ first and the abstract subject last. The stylist named draft 1’s line the worst of the portion (‘não será até o fim’ hangs until the subject comes; the order sounds carried over from the Latin) and proposed the subject first with ‘durará’. oblívio páuperis stays open between the poor man forgetting and being forgotten, as in the Latin; the blind reader heard ‘the poor is forgotten now, and that will end’ — the sense.

options.label: o esquecimento do pobre não será até o fim
options.note: Ruling since draft 2: the stylist’s order, the Latin’s verb (erit → será). Cost: ‘fim’ now ends both cola — the Latin’s own repetition of in finem, moved to the mediant by the order; accepted (the stylist asked that the repetition stay).

options.label: não será até o fim o esquecimento do pobre
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin’s order. The stylist’s worst line.

options.label: o esquecimento do pobre não durará até o fim
options.note: The stylist’s line: ‘durar’ for the copula is more than D2 lets the ear supply.

decisions.why: ἡτοίμασεν ἐν κρίσει τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ. Douay-Rheims 'He hath prepared his throne in judgment'; Matos Soares 1932 'para exercer o juízo'. In Brazil 'em juízo' is the lawyers' phrase for 'in court'.

options.label: em juízo
options.note: Ruling since draft 2, the Latinist’s (major): ‘para o juízo’ supplied a purpose the preposition does not state. ‘em juízo’ is the Latin’s preposition, and the court sense a Brazilian hears in it (a throne set up in judgment, in session) is the verse’s own; 118:154 has ‘em juízo’ too.

options.label: para o juízo
options.note: Draft 1 (Matos Soares 1932 without his ‘exercer’; the CNBB from the Hebrew): the Latinist marked the purpose major.

options.label: no juízo
options.note: To the letter; unclear what it says.

decisions.why: orbis terræ / terrárum: 17 verses (grep), several of them this very line (95:13 Judicábit orbem terræ in æquitáte, 97:9). 89:2 sets terra et orbis side by side, so orbis wants a word of its own. The Greek here is οἰκουμένη; Douay-Rheims 'the world'.

options.label: o orbe da terra
options.note: Ruling, proposed for the glossary. Both Latin words kept; 'orbe' is a dictionary word but lives in Catholic speech ('urbi et orbi', 'o orbe católico'). If the blind reader does not know it, 'o mundo' is the retreat.

options.label: o mundo
options.note: Douay-Rheims and the CNBB; plain, but it drops terræ and cannot serve 89:2 'terra et orbis'.

options.label: toda a terra
options.note: Matos Soares 1932; spends 'terra' and supplies 'toda' for orbis; collides with omnis terra (95:1, 96:9).

decisions.why: fíeri, factus est → fazer-se (glossary, open; Ps 117 'e se fez salvação para mim'); the row notes that it cannot serve where a state came upon someone. Here the Lord makes himself refuge — the row's own case. refúgium → refúgio; páuperi is a dative, kept with 'para' as the Ps 117 formula keeps 'mihi'.

options.label: E o Senhor se fez
options.note: Ruling; the glossary verb; Matos Soares 1932 has 'fez-se'.

options.label: E o Senhor tornou-se
options.note: The row's option.

options.label: E o Senhor foi
options.note: The CNBB's copula (from the Hebrew); loses the becoming.

decisions.why: Ps 9 has pauper ten times (9:10, 13, 19 twice, 23, 30a, 30b twice, 31, 33, 35b, 38; 45 lines in the psalter by grep) and húmilis once (9:39); elsewhere it stands beside inops (11:6a, 34:10, 36:14, 71:13, 73:21, 85:1, 112:7, 139:13), egénus (34:10, 40:2, 69:6, 81:3–4, 108:22) and húmilis (73:21, 81:3). The Latin has pauper for both πένης (9:10, 9:13, 9:19b) and πτωχός (9:19a, 9:23 …): one Latin word, one Portuguese word. The set proposed for the glossary: pauper → pobre, inops → indigente, egénus → necessitado, húmilis → humilde.

options.label: pobre
options.note: Ruling. What Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 have in nearly every place; plain; it keeps the number of each place (singular 9:10, 9:19a; plural 9:13, 9:19b).

options.label: pobre / infelizes (Matos Soares 1932)
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 varies in 9:19b; the Latin does not.

options.label: oprimido
options.note: The Diurnal's and the CNBB's word in 9:10 (Hebrew dak); not what pauper says.

decisions.why: ἐν εὐκαιρίαις: 'in seasonable times', at the right moments. The same phrase returns word for word in 9:22 (déspicis in opportunitátibus, in tribulatióne) and nowhere else in the psalter (grep), so the two must match. Douay-Rheims 'in due time'; Matos Soares 1932 'oportunamente'. adjútor → auxílio (glossary, open; Ps 117:6–7).

options.label: nas horas oportunas
options.note: Ruling. Keeps the plural and the adjective's root (opportúnus → oportuno); 'horas' supplies the noun Portuguese needs, as Douay-Rheims supplies 'time'.

options.label: no tempo oportuno
options.note: Douay-Rheims' singular; the commonest wording.

options.label: nas oportunidades
options.note: The cognate noun: in Brazil 'oportunidades' are chances, which is not the sense.

decisions.why: stúdia = τὰ ἐπιτηδεύματα, 'pursuits, practices, what one applies oneself to' (L&S studium: 'a busying one's self about a thing; zeal, endeavour'). Only one other verse: 13:1b 'abominábiles facti sunt in stúdiis suis' (grep), where it is men's evil practices. Douay-Rheims 'his ways'; Matos Soares 1932 'os seus desígnios'; the Diurnal and the CNBB 'feitos / obras' (the Hebrew's deeds).

options.label: os seus desígnios
options.note: Ruling. Matos Soares 1932's word: what someone sets himself to, which is the Latin's; it can serve 13:1b too (abomináveis nos seus desígnios). Cost: the doing is less heard than the intending.

options.label: os seus caminhos
options.note: Douay-Rheims; spends via's word.

options.label: os seus feitos
options.note: The Diurnal and the CNBB (from the Hebrew); what the deeds are, not what the Latin names.

options.label: os seus empenhos
options.note: Closest to L&S's 'endeavour'; not a word said of God.

decisions.latin: Quóniam requírens sánguinem eórum recordátus est
decisions.why: requírere sánguinem is the old idiom for calling a death to account (the Greek ἐκζητῶν τὰ αἵματα αὐτῶν); Douay-Rheims 'requiring their blood'. The glossary merged requírere into procurar at 118:145 (ἐκζητέω there too), but 'procurando o sangue deles' is heard as hunting for their blood — a sense the reverse of the Latin's. Whose blood (eórum) is not said: the Latin leaves it to the context (those who seek him, 9:11; the poor, 9:13b), and so does this. recordátus est has no object: kept absolute ('se lembrou').

options.label: ao pedir contas do sangue deles

forms.requirens: ao pedir contas do sangue deles

options.note: Ruling since draft 2. The idiom for the act (‘contas’ supplied to make it); the stylist’s shape — ‘ao’ + infinitive for the participle, and ‘ele’ named as subject (D2) so that the main verb has something to stand on. The blind reader heard ‘the Lord calls the victims’ death to account’ first.

options.label: pedindo contas do sangue deles
options.note: Draft 1 (with no ‘ele’): the stylist heard the intercalated clause hold back the verb with no subject to carry it.

options.label: ao procurar o sangue deles
options.note: The glossary’s verb for requírere / exquírere (118:145); heard as seeking to shed it.

options.label: ao requerer o sangue deles
options.note: The cognate, a legal claim; heard too as asking for blood to be given.

options.label: vingando o sangue deles
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and the CNBB’s ‘vingador’: the sense made explicit, and ulcísci’s verb.

decisions.why: humílitas / humiliáre → humilhação / humilhar (glossary, open; the row names 9:14 and 24:18 'vide humilitátem meam'). The Greek is ταπείνωσις, lowliness suffered; Douay-Rheims 'my humiliation'. 9:31 (second stage) has humiliábit.

options.label: a minha humilhação
options.note: Ruling: the glossary word, the family of 9:31's 'humilhará'.

options.label: o meu abatimento
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 ('o abatimento a que os meus inimigos me reduziram').

options.label: a minha humildade
options.note: Heard as the virtue.

decisions.why: ἐκ τῶν ἐχθρῶν μου: the humiliation that comes from the enemies. Douay-Rheims supplies a clause ('which I suffer from my enemies'), Matos Soares 1932 another ('a que os meus inimigos me reduziram'). Bare 'dos meus inimigos' would make the enemies the owners of the humiliation.

options.label: que me vem dos meus inimigos

forms.de_inimicis: que me vem dos meus inimigos

options.note: Ruling since draft 2, the stylist’s (who heard ‘humilhação vinda’ as clipped written prose): a clause, as Douay-Rheims’ (‘which I suffer from’) — here with the plainest verb, ‘vir’, that says only where it comes from. ‘a minha’ is kept (meam), which the stylist’s line dropped.

options.label: vinda dos meus inimigos
options.note: Draft 1: the participle of Ps 7:11 (‘vindo do Senhor’). The stylist: a clipped build of written prose.

options.label: que sofro dos meus inimigos
options.note: Douay-Rheims' clause; supplies a verb of suffering.

options.label: da parte dos meus inimigos
options.note: Plain and exact; heavier.

decisions.latin: Qui exáltas me de portis mortis
decisions.why: exaltáre → exaltar (glossary, working: 117:16 exaltávit me, 117:28a exaltábo te; 9:33 exaltétur manus tua in the second stage). Here it is local — lifting up out of the gates of death (ὁ ὑψῶν με ἐκ τῶν πυλῶν τοῦ θανάτου). 'Exaltar alguém' in Brazil is first to praise him; the spatial 'das portas da morte' corrects it within the colon. Douay-Rheims 'liftest me up'.

options.label: exaltais
options.note: Ruling: the glossary verb, so that 9:15 and 9:33 (exaltétur) are one verb as in the Latin.

options.label: levantais
options.note: Douay-Rheims 'liftest up', the Diurnal's 'levanta'; clear, but levantar-se is exsúrgere's (9:20, 9:33).

options.label: ergueis
options.note: Plain; erguer is kept for extóllere and astáre in the glossary.

decisions.why: infígere, passive: 'were fixed in, stuck fast' (ἐνεπάγησαν; Douay-Rheims 'have stuck fast'). Four places (grep): 9:16a, 37:3 sagíttæ tuæ infíxæ sunt mihi, 68:3 Infíxus sum in limo profúndi, 68:15 ut non infígar — arrows and mire. 'Presas' is not free: comprehénsus est → 'ficou preso' in the next two verses. Since draft 2 the subject comes first (the stylist: the inversion held it back) — order only (D2).

options.label: ficaram cravadas
options.note: Ruling. The concrete image of a thing driven in and held; serves the arrows of 37:3 exactly and the mire of 68:3 well enough.

options.label: fincaram-se
options.note: The same image, a more rustic verb.

options.label: atolaram-se
options.note: The plainest for being stuck fast (and for 68:3), but it supplies mud, and cannot serve 37:3.

options.label: caíram
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: loses the image.

decisions.why: intéritus (διαφθορά here): 8 verses (grep: 34:7, 48:11, 54:24, 102:4, 108:13, 139:12 …). Douay-Rheims 'destruction'; Matos Soares 1932 'ruína' — but ruína is a Latin word of its own (105:29, 109:6, 143:14).

options.label: destruição que fizeram
options.note: Ruling. Douay-Rheims’ noun; plain; free, since ruína has its own Latin word. fecérunt → ‘fizeram’ (ἐποίησαν): the Latin says they made it.

options.label: destruição que causaram
options.note: The stylist’s verb (‘fazer uma destruição’ is an unusual pairing). Refused: ‘causar’ is another verb; the Latin’s is fácere, the verb of 9:5 and 9:17, and the oddness is the Latin’s own.

options.label: ruína que fizeram
options.note: Matos Soares 1932; shorter and better sounding, but ruína is a Latin word of its own (105:29, 109:6, 143:14).

options.label: perdição que fizeram
options.note: Heard in Brazil as moral or eternal ruin.

decisions.why: comprehéndere → prender (glossary, open; Ps 7:6). The same form closes 9:16b and 9:17 (συνελήμφθη twice): it repeats. 'Foi preso' is what the police do; 'ficou preso' is being caught fast, which is the snare's image.

options.label: ficou preso
options.note: Ruling. The glossary verb in the stative passive Portuguese uses for a trap (Matos Soares 1932 and the CNBB have it in 9:16b); the repetition kept.

options.label: foi preso
options.note: The passive to the letter; heard as arrested.

options.label: foi apanhado
options.note: The CNBB's verb in 9:17; leaves the glossary's prender.

decisions.why: κρίματα ποιῶν: carrying out judgments. Douay-Rheims 'when he executeth judgments'; Matos Soares 1932 'faz justiça'. fácere judícium is an open row (118:84 'fazer juízo sobre', 118:121 'praticar o juízo'); bare 'fazendo juízos' is heard as forming opinions.

options.label: ao executar juízos
options.note: Ruling since draft 2. ‘executar’ is the verb a Portuguese ear gives to a judgment carried out (Douay-Rheims ‘executeth’); judícia → juízos (D15), plural kept. ‘ao’ + infinitive for the participle is the stylist’s (the bare gerund left the tie loose) — grammar. The blind reader heard ‘applying sentences’ first, ‘deciding causes’ second: both are κρίματα.

options.label: executando juízos
options.note: Draft 1: the participle as a gerund.

options.label: ao fazer juízos
options.note: The calque; heard as forming opinions.

options.label: ao praticar juízos
options.note: 118:121’s verb; praticar is operári’s in the glossary.

options.label: fazendo justiça
options.note: Matos Soares 1932; spends justítia’s word.

decisions.latin: in opéribus mánuum suárum comprehénsus est peccátor
decisions.why: suárum is reflexive: the sinner's own hands. In the Latin's order the Portuguese 'das suas mãos' comes before its owner, right after 'o Senhor' of the first colon, and is heard as the Lord's hands. Matos Soares 1932 inserts '(próprias)'.

options.label: o pecador ficou preso nas obras das suas mãos

forms.v17b: o pecador {comprehensus} nas obras das suas mãos

options.note: Ruling. Subject first — order only (D2) — so 'suas' has its owner before it.

options.label: nas obras das suas mãos ficou preso o pecador

forms.v17b: nas obras das suas mãos {comprehensus} o pecador

options.note: The Latin's order; 'suas' is heard as the Lord's.

options.label: nas obras das suas próprias mãos ficou preso o pecador

forms.v17b: nas obras das suas próprias mãos {comprehensus} o pecador

options.note: Matos Soares 1932's gloss taken into the text; 'próprias' is supplied.

decisions.why: convértere → voltar (glossary), the verb of 9:4 (In converténdo … retrórsum): the enemies who were turned back are now turned into the underworld (ἀποστραφήτωσαν … εἰς τὸν ᾅδην). Ps 6:11 has convertántur → 'que se voltem', with no place named; with 'in' + a place 'voltar-se para' would be 'face towards'. Douay-Rheims 'shall be turned into hell'; Matos Soares 1932 'Sejam precipitados'.

options.label: Voltem
options.note: Ruling. 'Voltar para' is 'go back to', which is what the Greek's verb says; the jussive subjunctive, as the Latin; one verb with 9:4.

options.label: Sejam voltados
options.note: The passive to the letter (Douay-Rheims); heavy.

options.label: Voltem-se
options.note: Ps 6:11's form; with 'para o inferno' heard as turning to face it.

options.label: Sejam lançados
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's sense ('precipitados'); another verb.

decisions.why: inférnus → inferno (glossary, open; D22 holds it for Gustavo's ear; 19 verses). The Greek is ᾅδης, the world of the dead. The blind reader of Ps 6 heard the hell of the damned first. Here, of sinners and nations that forget God, that hearing is the traditional one (Matos Soares 1932 'no inferno', with his footnote 'isto é, na habitação dos mortos'; Douay-Rheims 'into hell').

options.label: o inferno
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word, as Ps 6:6; both Vulgate-family versions have it.

options.label: os infernos
options.note: The old plural for the abode of the dead (the Creed's wording — from memory, unverified).

options.label: a mansão dos mortos
options.note: A paraphrase (the Creed as now said in Brazil — unverified).

options.label: a habitação dos mortos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's footnote.

decisions.why: confortári = be strengthened (μὴ κραταιούσθω). 12 verses have the stem (grep: 26:14 and 30:25 et confortétur cor, 17:18, 68:5, 141:7 confortáti sunt super me, 138:17 …). Douay-Rheims 'let not man be strengthened'; Matos Soares 1932 'não triunfe'; the Diurnal and the CNBB 'não prevaleça' (from the Hebrew).

options.label: se fortaleça
options.note: Ruling, proposed for the glossary: confortári → fortalecer-se. The Latin's verb; it will serve 26:14 (e fortaleça-se o vosso coração) and the enemies 'fortalecidos contra mim' of 17:18, 141:7.

options.label: prevaleça
options.note: The Diurnal and the CNBB (from the Hebrew): the outcome of being strong, not the Latin's word.

options.label: triunfe
options.note: Matos Soares 1932.

decisions.why: in conspéctu → à vista de (glossary, open: proposed in Ps 5:9, 51 verses; Ps 118:168–170 found that it fails with verbs of motion and used 'a vossa presença'). Here the verb is a passive of judging, no motion. 9:26a (second stage) has 'in conspéctu ejus'.

options.label: à vossa vista
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's proposal, which holds where there is no motion.

options.label: na vossa presença
options.note: Matos Soares 1932; Ps 118:168–170.

options.label: diante de vós
options.note: Plain; loses the noun.

decisions.why: νομοθέτην: the Latin and Greek read a lawgiver where the Hebrew has 'fear' (the Diurnal: 'o teu terror'). One other verse: 83:8 benedictiónem dabit legislátor (grep). In Brazil 'legislador' is first a member of parliament. super eos is masculine though gentes is feminine (ad sensum, the nations as men, as the verse ends): kept as 'sobre eles'.

options.label: um legislador
options.note: Ruling. The Latin's reading, with Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932; the parliamentary echo is a cost, but a plain one, and the verse corrects it ('para que saibam que são homens').

options.label: um que lhes dê a lei

forms.legislatorem: um que lhes dê a lei

options.note: Unpacks the compound; a clause for a noun.

options.label: um mestre
options.note: A Hebrew-family sense (moreh, 'teacher'): refused under rule 1.

choices.9:2: The psalm begins at 9:2 (9:1 is the titulus; D7). in toto corde meo → 'de todo o meu coração' (glossary formula). narráre → narrar; mirabília → maravilhas (the family of mirábilis → maravilhoso).
choices.9:3: lætári / exsultáre → alegrar-se / exultar (glossary). 'Eu me alegrarei' supplies the subject pronoun so that the verse does not open on a clitic; 'Alegrar-me-ei' (Matos Soares 1932) is the mesóclise the brief keeps for where it reads naturally. 'em vós' closes the colon and governs both verbs, as in te does.
choices.9:4: infirmári → enfraquecer (glossary row infírmus). The verbs are plural after a singular 'inimigo', as in the Latin and the Greek: the enemy is a host.
choices.9:5: sedísti → 'sentastes-vos' (enclisis at the head of a clause); super thronum → 'sobre o trono' (glossary super, place).
choices.9:6: ímpius → ímpio; delére → apagar (Douay-Rheims 'blotted out', Matos Soares 1932 'apagaste'). eórum → 'deles', not 'o seu nome', which after 'o ímpio' would point to him alone — and in Brazil 'seu' is also 'your'. The last colon is long (the Latin's twenty syllables against about twenty-three) and ends on 'séculos', a proparoxytone, as the Latin ends on sǽculi: the formula is kept whole.
choices.9:7a: frámea → espada (ῥομφαία, Douay-Rheims 'swords'). inimíci read as a genitive singular with the Greek. destrúere → destruir (glossary; not an imperative). The Latin's order 'et civitátes eórum destruxísti' becomes the natural Portuguese one.
choices.9:7b: sónitus → 'estrondo' (Douay-Rheims 'with a noise'; Matos Soares 1932 'ruído'). The inline marker (8a) is not reproduced. permanére → permanecer.
choices.9:8b: The inline marker (9) is not reproduced. ipse → 'ele mesmo' (Matos Soares 1932). ǽquitas → equidade (glossary). The Latin swaps the Greek's pair (the world in equity, the peoples in justice): the Latin's order is followed. in + ablative → 'com' (manner), as Matos Soares 1932.
choices.9:10: adjútor → auxílio (glossary, open; Ps 117:6–7 'o meu auxílio'); tribulátio → tribulação.
choices.9:11: speráre in → esperar em; novísse → conhecer; derelínquere → abandonar; quǽrere → buscar (all glossary).
choices.9:12: psállere → entoar salmos (D25), at the vós imperative (entoai; past entoei — safe). annuntiáre → anunciar (glossary note on prædicáre); anunciai is safe. The Latin's colon at the end of the verse is kept: 9:13 gives the reason.
choices.9:13: clamor → clamor; oblivísci → esquecer with a direct object (glossary). 'se lembrou' closes the colon on an oxytone.
choices.9:14: Miserére mei → 'Tende piedade de mim' (glossary formula). vide → 'vede' (safe: past 'vi').
choices.9:15: The verse hangs on 9:14's address, as the Latin does (Qui exáltas me … ut annúntiem): no main verb is supplied. laudátio → louvor (the family of laus). portæ repeats (portis mortis … in portis fíliæ Sion), as in the Latin.
choices.9:16a: salutáre → salvação (D6). The Latin's order (verb first) kept.
choices.9:18: oblivísci Deum → 'esquecem a Deus' (the preposition Portuguese puts before 'Deus' as object).
choices.9:19: oblívio páuperis → 'o esquecimento do pobre': open, as the Latin is, between the poor man forgetting and being forgotten. patiéntia → paciência (Douay-Rheims 'patience'), not the Hebrew family's 'esperança'. The repetition 'até o fim … até o fim' is the Latin's (decision in_finem).
choices.9:20: 'Exsúrge, Dómine' → 'Levantai-vos, Senhor' (glossary formula; 9:33 again). homo → homem.
choices.9:21: constitúere → estabelecer (glossary; 'Estabelecei' is safe: past 'estabeleci'). scire → saber before a 'que' clause (the glossary's scire row: Portuguese collocation decides). The first stage ends here, where Hebrew Ps 9 ends.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm9.txt, 42 prayed verses 9:2–9:39 with DO's split ids (9:7a, 9:7b, 9:8b, 9:16a, 9:16b, 9:26a, 9:26b, 9:30a, 9:30b, 9:35a, 9:35b) and two inline markers in 9:7b and 9:8b, (8a) and (9), not reproduced. One '*' per verse. 9:1 is the titulus (D7). Worked in two stages in one folder, as Ps 118 was: 9:2–9:21 (Hebrew Ps 9) first, then 9:22–9:39 (Hebrew Ps 10) appended. While partial, prayed.json and literal.json carry 'range'; ps009/partial.py (from ps118/partial.py) stands in for checks.py, ps009/part.py (from ps118/part3.py) builds the critics' sub-folder for the second stage. The previous agent left only ps009/consult/ (two Douay-Rheims fetches, kept) and an empty critic/.

Stage one (9:2–9:21), draft 1, from consult/parallels/ps009.md (Douay-Rheims chapters regenerated by the coordinator; the Matos Soares 1932 text layer; the Diurnal Monástico 1962 and the CNBB for diction only; DO's Portuguese not used, D12). Lewis & Short read for studium. Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: 9:10b = 9:22b (in opportunitátibus, in tribulatióne); 9:6 increpásti = 118:21; 9:2 = 110:1, 137:1 (first colon); in finem ×3 against in ætérnum ×2 in these twenty verses; orbem terræ in æquitáte = 95:13. Rule 3 checked at every vós imperative: Entoai, anunciai, Tende, vede, Levantai-vos, Estabelecei — all safe. Glossary applied: D5 (dar graças), D6 (salvação), D23 (para sempre), D25 (entoar salmos), D15 (juízo), convértere → voltar (9:4, 9:18, one verb), increpáre → repreender (tested, holds), humílitas → humilhação, exaltáre → exaltar, comprehéndere → prender, inférnus → inferno (for Gustavo), in conspéctu → à vista de. Proposed: in finem → até o fim, pauper → pobre (and the set inops / egénus / húmilis), orbis terræ → o orbe da terra, confortári → fortalecer-se, stúdia → desígnios, intéritus → destruição, infígere → ficar cravado. Places where the Latin follows the Greek against the Hebrew and is followed: 9:8b the Latin's swapped pair, 9:13 requírens, 9:19 patiéntia, 9:20 non confortétur, 9:21 legislatórem.

Stage one, draft 1, through ps009/partial.py (checks.py's own code on 9:2–9:21): hard pass (ids and marks). Soft flags, all accepted: 9:3 both cola long (+3, +5: 'Eu me' supplied, and D25's two words 'entoarei salmos' for psallam); 9:4b +3, 9:6b +3 (the doxology formula, which ends on 'séculos' as the Latin on sǽculi), 9:7a first colon +4 (articles and 'até o fim'), 9:11 first colon +3, 9:12 first colon +3 (entoai salmos again), 9:15 second colon +3, 9:16a second colon +3, 9:17 first colon +3 (the gerund 'executando'); 9:10b −3 and 9:13a −3 and 9:17b −4 (Latin polysyllables: opportunitátibus, requírens sánguinem, opéribus mánuum). No cadence flag: every Portuguese colon ends oxytone or paroxytone. No rhyme flag.

Stage one, draft 1 (9:2–9:21). Four verses: two majors, both taken (9:4 the gerund's accusative, with the future passive inside the same remark; 9:8b 'para o juízo'); two minors refused under the glossary (9:6 the singular 'século do século', 9:10 'auxiliador'). Marks confirmed in all 21 verses. Passed without remark: 'fizestes valer o meu juízo', 'julgais a justiça', 'Repreendestes', 'desfaleceram até o fim', 'o orbe da terra', 'pedindo contas do sangue', 'ficaram cravadas', 'ficou preso', 'executando juízos', 'Voltem … para o inferno', 'não se fortaleça', 'à vossa vista', 'um legislador'.

outcomes.remark: the active gerund has inimícum meum as its OBJECT: it is making the enemy turn back; 'Ao voltar para trás o meu inimigo' makes him the subject (MAJOR) → 'Ao fazer voltar para trás o meu inimigo'
outcomes.reason: Right on the Latin's grammar; 'fazer voltar' still names no agent.

outcomes.remark: infirmabúntur is passive → 'serão enfraquecidos'
outcomes.reason: Voice is kept (the brief). Cost: the colon is five syllables over.

outcomes.remark: 'pelos séculos dos séculos' pluralises the Latin's singular → 'pelo século do século' (minor)
outcomes.reason: The glossary formula (asked and refused the same way at 118:44); the singular is not said in Portuguese prayer, and both Vulgate-family versions have the plural.

outcomes.remark: 'in judício' places the preparing in judgment; 'para o juízo' introduces a purpose (MAJOR) → 'em juízo'
outcomes.reason: Right: the preposition was interpreted. The court sense of 'em juízo' is the verse's own.

outcomes.remark: adjútor names the one who helps; 'auxílio' is a defensible metonymy → 'auxiliador' (minor)
outcomes.reason: The glossary row adjútor → auxílio (Ps 117:6–7; 118:114 held against three readings), the same metonymy as suscéptor → amparo; 'auxiliador' is long and rare.

audit.note: Stage one, draft 1. Eight verses; best 9:7b, worst 9:19. 'O salmo tem sobriedade e uma voz de oração reconhecível, com imagens fortes e boas terminações … a repetição de «até o fim» deve permanecer, pois pertence ao próprio latim.' Five taken (9:3, 9:13, 9:14, 9:17 whole or nearly; 9:16a and 9:19 by order with the Latin's verb kept), one overtaken by the Latinist (9:4), one refused and kept as an option (9:6).

outcomes.remark: the vocative parts the singing from its object → 'Altíssimo, entoarei salmos ao vosso nome'
outcomes.reason: Order only (D2).

outcomes.remark: the subject comes late after 'voltar para trás' → 'Quando o meu inimigo voltar para trás'
outcomes.reason: Overtaken by the Latinist's major: the enemy is the gerund's object, not the subject; 'Ao fazer voltar' has no late subject to wait for.

outcomes.remark: 'séculos' ends the verse proparoxytone → 'pelos séculos dos séculos, e para sempre'
outcomes.reason: It reverses the Latin's two members; the Latin ends on the proparoxytone sǽculi too; formulas stay whole.

outcomes.remark: the intercalated clause holds back the main verb, which has no expressed subject → 'Porque, ao pedir contas do sangue deles, ele se lembrou'
outcomes.reason: Grammar and a named subject (D2).

outcomes.remark: 'humilhação vinda' is clipped written prose → 'a humilhação que me vem dos meus inimigos'
outcomes.reason: A clause for the participle, as Douay-Rheims; 'a minha' kept for meam.

outcomes.remark: the inversion holds back the subject, and 'fazer uma destruição' is an unusual pairing → 'as nações ficaram cravadas na destruição que causaram'
outcomes.reason: The order is taken; 'causaram' is refused — fecérunt is fácere, and the oddness is the Latin's. Kept as an option.

outcomes.remark: the bare gerund after 'será conhecido' leaves the tie loose → 'ao executar juízos'
outcomes.reason: Grammar (D2).

outcomes.remark: 'não será até o fim' hangs until the abstract subject; carried-over order (WORST LINE) → 'Porque o esquecimento do pobre não durará até o fim'
outcomes.reason: The order is taken; 'durará' for erit is refused (more than a supplied copula) and kept as an option.

audit.note: Stage one, draft 1, Portuguese only. 28 items, 3 unknown words (orbe, equidade, desígnios). Almost everything is the Latin's own range heard as the Latin is read: whose name, cities and memory (deles), the enemy as a host (plural verbs), whose blood (9:13), 'filha de Sião' heard as a woman, homo as 'the male'. The legal readings were heard right first: 9:5 'the Lord gave the speaker right', 9:13 'the Lord calls the victims' death to account', 9:17 'applying sentences'. No change made on its account; 9:4 changed for the Latinist.

outcomes.remark: 'fizestes valer o meu juízo': made my opinion prevail / made good the judgment on my cause
outcomes.reason: The right reading was heard first ('O Senhor deu razão a quem fala'); the verb is there to make it so.

outcomes.remark: 'julgais a justiça': judge justice itself / judge causes justly
outcomes.reason: The Latin's own oddness; the right sense was heard first.

outcomes.remark: 'deles': the poor / the nations / other victims
outcomes.reason: The Latin's eórum is as open; the listener settles on the poor by the verse's end, as a Latin reader does.

outcomes.remark: 'a filha de Sião' can sound like a woman; the city is not explained
outcomes.reason: The Latin's image (rule 5); no footnote in the text.

outcomes.remark: 'Voltem … para o inferno' suggests a return to a place they had been
outcomes.reason: The Greek's verb is 'turn back' (ἀποστρέφω, as in 9:4 εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω), and the psalm ties the two verses; the likely hearing was 'be sent to hell'.

outcomes.remark: 'não perecerá até o fim': will not be lost for ever / will last until the end and may end then
outcomes.reason: The Latin's in finem is as open; kept apart from in ætérnum. Evidence recorded on the glossary row.

outcomes.remark: 'o homem': humankind / one man / males
outcomes.reason: homo; the right sense heard first.

outcomes.remark: unknown word 'orbe'
outcomes.reason: Kept as the glossary proposal ('o mundo' is the retreat); recorded on the new open row for the main session.

outcomes.remark: unknown word 'equidade'
outcomes.reason: Glossary (ǽquitas → equidade, working); the Ps 118 blind reader listed it too.

outcomes.remark: unknown word 'desígnios' (yet heard as 'the Lord's plans')
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; kept.

audit.note: Stage one, draft 2 (revise_v2.py; draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json). Latinist: 9:4 'Ao fazer voltar para trás o meu inimigo: * serão enfraquecidos', 9:8b 'em juízo'. Stylist: 9:3 vocative first, 9:13 'ao pedir … ele se lembrou', 9:14 'que me vem dos meus inimigos', 9:16a subject first, 9:17 'ao executar juízos', 9:19 subject first with 'será'. New decisions infirmabuntur and v19a; saeculi now takes the whole phrase so that the stylist's reversal can be shown. Checks (partial.py): hard pass; new soft flags 9:4b +5 (the passive; accepted) and 9:17a +4; no rhyme flag, though 9:19 now ends both cola on 'fim' — the Latin's repetition.
